title: Sormano and de Vaulx to François I, Ferrara, February 1529, BnF fr. 3096 nos. 63, 65, 66

steps.what: Checked Lasry's key against the interlinear decipherment of control no. 62.
Segmented, clustered, hand-labelled and k-NN-classified the glyphs; checked every line by eye.
Applied the key; found a null, crossbarred long-s = e and the duca sign on the leaves.
Aligned nos. 65 and 66, which encipher different passages, as a mutual crib.
Read nos. 65 and 66 in full and no. 63 as far as its leaves go.

Contribution re-assessed on Lasry's note (21 Sept 2026): the key serves the whole volume, and checking for a shared key within one collection is standard, so this is not a key found elsewhere. The main achievement is transcription. The same cipher is in fr. 3045 f. 28 and fr. 3034 f. 154 (not read here).

(Arya Sanketbhai Patel, former entry sormano1529, PR #2) Piece list corrected on the leaves: no. 63's third sheet is f. 123, dated penultimo February 1529 (27 Feb), signed Sormano and Joachin; no. 64 has no cipher; 'Ioachin' identified as Gian Gioacchino de Passano, seigneur de Vaux; Molini prints none of nos. 63, 65, 66.

(Patel) Eight attempts to recover the key from the microfilm without a key (mask overlap, cosine, nearest template, NCC, eye, LM Viterbi, hybrid boxes) failed on homophone forms the film does not separate; from the f. 124 margin crib and the f. 113 gloss he derived 22 values, of which 20 agree with Lasry's table once it was found.

One-key review (Lasry's rule, 14 Oct 2026): the two entries for this one key and these three letters (sormano, sormano1529) merged into this one; outcome reconciled per document: nos. 65 and 66 read, no. 63 read in part, so the entry is read in part.

f. 123r, the third sheet of no. 63, deciphered with Lasry's key and the KEY.md corrections: seven cipher runs, about 386 of 389 glyphs into Italian (end of the Naples/captaincy passage; postscript: letters from Rome of the 18th report the Pope relapsed, the French cardinals to prepare for a conclave). Three signs before 'ricaduto' give no word. The crossbarred long-s acts as a null here.

Full texts listed in outcome.texts (George Lasry's request of 22 Oct 2026): per letter, the line-by-line transcriptions with their glyph-level XML and the readings (n63 with the f. 123r sheet); Patel's (arya) separate reading of no. 65's Duke's answer and his clear-text transcriptions; key = KEY.md with the corrections made here, beside Lasry's published table key_lasry3.png.

Reading audit (George Lasry's sentence test, 22 Oct 2026): n65_reading.md, n66_reading.md, n63_reading.md and n63_f123r_reading.md read through. No. 65 reads as Italian sentences (reviewed B) and no. 63 f. 123r's three runs read (split off, reviewed B); no. 66's own cipher stretches are left 《…》 and no. 63 ff. 115-116 have holes in nearly every sentence: relabelled decoded, not read. fraction_read unknown -> ~0.5 (estimated by glyphs).

Re-read (batch b23): IIIF info.json for the volume gives 8653 x 5877 per opening, the same master as the raw/ captures used since September; a max-size crop differs from the raw crop only by re-encoding. No better image exists online. No DECODE record, and no decipherment of nos. 63/66 on Tomokiyo's or Lasry's pages.

No. 66 ff. 121r-122r: every cipher stretch re-read sign by sign on full-resolution strips; the old f. 121r strings were misreadings, f. 121v L21-43 and f. 122r had never been transcribed. Reads as Italian throughout (no66_reading.md, 0.753 clean, HOLES=1 0.989).

Values holding across no. 66: crossbarred long-s is a null (~20 places; also on f. 123r, against KEY.md's e from f. 113r, not changed); looped b-shaped sign = rr (ridure, Ferara, l'errore; no. 65 ridu{B}e, le {B}ore); looped Z = z (speranza, excelenza, contenteza). Code sign V-with-stroke+e read Papa from four contexts and a curled saltire ?Imperatore from one: flagged as sense-only.

No. 63 f. 115r lines 1-27 re-read with the same values (quello niente che in sin allhora ... non esser da far gran fondamento che sua excelenza veramente dovesi [...] ben risoluta accettarlo); about 20 signs unread. The rest of ff. 115-116 not reached in the session.

Consistency pass (cl): outcome.gaps no. 65 line illegible -> not-attempted, as NOTES already says (the signs are legible); the closed no. 66 line moved out of the open list; NOTES Status read in part -> in progress (no. 63 from f. 115r l. 28 and no. 65 still to re-read).

outcome.method_basis: Lasry's 2023 key for BnF fr. 3096 (on Tomokiyo's cryptiana) was verified against the interlinear decipherment of no. 62 and the margin of no. 67 and applied to nos. 63, 65 and 66 after a glyph transcription; nos. 65 and 66 encipher different passages and served as mutual cribs.
outcome.notes: Merged 14 Oct 2026 with sormano1529 (same key, same letters). Nos. 65 and 66 read; no. 63 read in part: the long runs of ff. 115v-116r in patches, its third sheet f. 123r read. Lasry's key gains a null, a duca sign and four letter forms. 22 Oct 2026, reading audit: no. 65 and no. 63 f. 123r read; no. 66's own cipher stretches and no. 63 ff. 115-116 are decoded, not read.

texts.label: No. 65, BnF fr. 3096 ff. 119-120, Sormano and de Vaulx (Passano) to François I, Ferrara, 23 Feb 1529
texts.summary: The French envoys at Ferrara to François I on their audience with Alfonso I d'Este, duke of Ferrara, after the reverence to Madama Renée and Don Ercole: the duke refuses to take the kingdom of Naples for himself or the captaincy of the French army, offers only to accept whatever accord the King negotiates for him with the Pope, and pleads the want of provisions; the agents judge his difficulties pretexts and fall back on Ercole and on Trivulzio. arya/ct/read_no65_duke_answer.md is Patel's separate reading of the Duke's answer (f. 119v) with Lasry's key, controlled on the clear twin no. 66.

reading_review.note: n65_reading.md, 'Continuous reading of the whole letter': the deciphered stretches join the clear text into Italian sentences (we persuaded, comforted and urged his Lordship to accept the enterprise of Naples on the conditions of the instruction; he refused the kingdom for himself) with a few ... and one partly legible run (f. 119r L32-36). Audit grade C refined for no. 65.

texts.label: No. 66, BnF fr. 3096 ff. 121-122, the 'duplicata' of no. 65, Ferrara, 23 Feb 1529
texts.summary: The independently drafted duplicate of no. 65, which writes in clear many of the passages no. 65 enciphers and the reverse, so that the pair cribs each other; it opens with Gian Gioacchino de Passano's arrival at the lodging of the ambassador Gaspare Sormano. arya/ct/clear_texts.md holds Patel's transcription of the clear passages of nos. 63, 65, 66 and 67.

reading_review.note: no66_reading.md: every cipher stretch of ff. 121r-122r re-read sign by sign on the IIIF master with Lasry's key plus values that hold across the document (crossbarred long-s null ~20x; looped b-sign = rr: ridure, Ferara, l'errore; looped Z = z); no. 65 used as a check only. Clean-sentence share 0.753 (HOLES=1 0.989), was 0.316. Code signs [Papa] (4 contexts) and [?Imperatore] (1) identified from context only, flagged; 13 look-alike letters. Log no66_reread_log.md.

texts.label: No. 63, BnF fr. 3096 ff. 115-116 and 123, Ferrara, 27 Feb 1529: ff. 115-116
texts.summary: The follow-up to the duplicate pair of 23 February, the most heavily enciphered of the three; its third sheet f. 123r, bound out of order and dated 'penultimo de Febraro', ends the letter on Naples and the captaincy, and its postscript reports from Rome that the Pope has relapsed, 'sensa speransa di salute', and that the French cardinals should make ready for a conclave.
texts.note: ff. 115-116 re-read 23 Oct 2026 (batch b23) only as far as f. 115r line 27 (no63_reading.md, partial: 0.50 clean, HOLES=1 0.95; log no63_reread_log.md). The leaf is legible on the IIIF master and reads with Lasry's key and no. 66's values; the rest of f. 115r and ff. 115v-116v (about 2,500 signs) are not yet re-read. Blocker: not-attempted (session time), not illegibility.

texts.label: No. 63, BnF fr. 3096 ff. 115-116 and 123, Ferrara, 27 Feb 1529: f. 123r (third sheet)

reading_review.note: n63_f123r_reading.md: the three cipher runs of f. 123r are read glyph by glyph (about 386 of 389) into Italian that continues the clear text ('a l'impresa de Napoli, ne anche al capitaneato, mediante il quale quando l'havese accetato o accetase ... conduta la pratica de la'); one three-sign group gives no word.
